Build an OpenAlex request (httr2)

Source: R/pro_query.R
pro_query.Rd

Construct an httr2 request for the OpenAlex API. All filters must be supplied as named ... arguments (e.g., from_publication_date = "2020-01-01").

Usage

pro_query(
  entity = c("works", "authors", "venues", "institutions", "concepts", "publishers",
    "funders", "sources", "topics", "locations"),
  id = NULL,
  doi = NULL,
  search = NULL,
  search.exact = NULL,
  search.semantic = NULL,
  group_by = NULL,
  select = NULL,
  options = NULL,
  endpoint = "https://api.openalex.org",
  chunk_limit = 50L,
  oql = NULL,
  oqo = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

entity

Character; one of "works", "authors", "institutions", "publishers", "funders", "sources", "topics", "locations". "venues" (now "sources") and "concepts" (now "topics") are deprecated by OpenAlex and kept only for compatibility.

id

Optional ID or vector of IDs (e.g., "W1775749144"). If a single ID is provided, fetches one entity directly. If multiple IDs are provided, they are automatically moved into the ids.openalex filter.

doi

Optional DOI or vector of DOIs (e.g., "10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2"). Values are moved into the doi filter and automatically chunked into separate requests when the number of DOIs exceeds chunk_limit.

search

Optional full-text search string. Applies stemming and stop-word removal. Supports boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT in uppercase), quoted phrases ("exact phrase") and proximity ("word1 word2"~N). Wildcards are rejected by the API (HTTP 400): use search.exact. Replaces the deprecated filter = field.search:keyword syntax.

search.exact

Optional full-text search without stemming or stop-word removal. Supports the boolean/phrase/proximity syntax of search, plus wildcards and fuzzy matching. Use when you need to match exact word forms (e.g. "surgery" should not match "surgical").

search.semantic

Optional semantic (AI-powered) search string. Uses embeddings to match conceptual meaning rather than exact keywords. Limited to 1 request per second and returns at most 50 results per query.

group_by

Optional field to group by (facets), e.g. "type".

select

Optional character vector of fields to return.

options

Optional named list of additional query parameters (e.g., list(sort = "cited_by_count:desc", sample = 100, seed = 42)). pro_request() does the paging, so page and cursor given here are replaced (with a warning); per_page is kept (1–200, default 200). A sample (up to 10,000) is paged by page number and needs a seed when it spans several pages; pro_request() picks and reports one if none is given.

endpoint

Base API URL. Defaults to "https://api.openalex.org".

chunk_limit

Number of DOIS or ids per chunk if chunked. Default: 50

oql

Optional OQL (OpenAlex Query Language) query string, e.g. "works where year is (2020) and type is (article)". A character vector gives a named list of URLs (names from names(oql), else query_1, query_2, ...), one per query. See section OQL and OQO.

oqo

Optional OQO (OpenAlex Query Object): a nested list, or a JSON string. A list of OQOs (lists or JSON strings), or a character vector of JSON strings, gives a named list of URLs as for oql. See section OQL and OQO.

...

Filters as named arguments. Values may be scalars or vectors (vectors are collapsed with "|" to express OR). Arguments of the functions that send the query, such as via or workers, belong to [pro_fetch()], [pro_request()] or [pro_count()], not here.

Value

An individual URL or a list of URLs.

Details

Filter names are validated against opt_filter_names(entity = entity) and select fields against opt_select_fields(entity = entity), i.e. against the names OpenAlex accepts for the queried entity.

If multiple more then 50 `doi` or openalex `id`s are provided, the request is automatically split into chunks of 50 and a named list of URLs is returned.

Search syntax

All three search parameters (search, search.exact, search.semantic) accept a query string. For search and search.exact, the following syntax is supported:

  • Boolean: biodiversity AND finance, climate OR weather, ocean NOT pollution (operators must be uppercase); group with parentheses. Words without an operator between them are combined with AND.

  • Exact phrase: "biodiversity finance" (double quotes).

  • Proximity: "biodiversity finance"~5 (words within 5 positions), or two phrases near each other: "machine learning"~5~"neural network".

Only with search.exact (the stemmed search rejects wildcards with HTTP 400, and stemming distorts fuzzy terms):

  • Wildcard: microbio* (zero or more characters), organi?ation (exactly one). At least 3 characters before the wildcard; no leading wildcard.

  • Fuzzy: biodiversty~1 (up to N character edits, N = 0–2; at least 3 characters before the ~).

See https://help.openalex.org/api/searching/. search.semantic does not use keyword syntax; pass a natural-language phrase or even a full abstract. It returns at most 50 results per call.

OQL and OQO

OpenAlex's query language (oql) and its JSON form (oqo) express queries the classic filter syntax cannot, such as nested and / or conditions. The entity, all conditions, grouping (group by), sample and corpus belong inside the query, so entity, id, doi, the search arguments, group_by and filters in ... cannot be combined with it – OpenAlex would silently ignore them. select and options (e.g. sort) are passed alongside. The URL targets the API root (https://api.openalex.org/?oql=...) and works with pro_request(), pro_count() and pro_fetch() as usual. An invalid query fails at request time with OpenAlex's parse error. See https://help.openalex.org/api/oql/.

Deprecated search filters

Filter arguments with a .search suffix (e.g. title_and_abstract.search = "biodiversity") are deprecated by the OpenAlex API. They still work but emit a warning. Use the search, search.exact, or search.semantic parameters instead. See https://help.openalex.org/api/searching/ for details.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

url <- pro_query(
  entity = "works",
  search = "biodiversity",
  from_publication_date = "2020-01-01",
  language = c("en","de"),
  select = c("id","title","publication_year"),
  options = list(per_page = 5)
)

# OQL: nested conditions the filter syntax cannot express
url <- pro_query(
  oql = "works where year >= (2020) and (title has (coral) or title has (reef))"
)

# OQO: the same kind of query as a nested list
url <- pro_query(oqo = list(
  get_rows = "works",
  filter_rows = list(list(column_id = "publication_year", value = 2020))
))
} # }
